recognize_zh: 同一張骨髓抹片加上標示：黑色箭頭為細胞核偏心、藍色細胞質豐富並有核周淡染區的漿細胞；紅色箭頭為細胞核圓而置中、染色質極致密、細胞質僅一圈的晚期紅血球前驅細胞。
features: Black arrows: plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, abundant basophilic cytoplasm and perinuclear hof
Red arrows: late (polychromatic/orthochromatic) normoblasts with central, round, dense pyknotic-appearing nuclei
Normoblasts with narrow rim of grey-blue to pinkish cytoplasm and no hof
Plasma cells larger with coarse 'clock-face' chromatin
Background granulocytic precursors and segmented neutrophils
describe_en: Annotated bone marrow aspirate smear demonstrates plasma cells (black arrows) with eccentric nuclei, coarse chromatin, abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm and a perinuclear hof, contrasted with late erythroid precursors (red arrows) that are smaller with centrally located, round, very dense nuclei and a thin rim of polychromatic cytoplasm without a hof. Granulocytic precursors are present in the background. The image illustrates how nuclear position, chromatin density and the Golgi hof distinguish plasma cells from normoblasts.

ddx.vs: Basophilic normoblasts have a central nucleus with deep blue cytoplasm but no localized Golgi hof, whereas plasma cells have an eccentric nucleus with an adjacent hof.
Orthochromatic normoblasts have a very dense, round, homogeneous nucleus with pinkish hemoglobinized cytoplasm, while lymphocytes have slightly less dense chromatin and pale blue cytoplasm.
Plasmacytoid lymphocytes have less abundant cytoplasm and lymphocyte-like chromatin with a less distinct hof.
